title: Points, Lines, Rays, Angles
description: Learn points, lines, line segments, rays and angles for Class 3. Classify right, acute and obtuse angles. Free online tests and IMO practice questions.

topics.title: Point, Line Segment, Ray, and Angle
topics.concept:
Geometry starts with basic building blocks:

  • Point: An exact location in space (shown as a dot •)
  • Line segment: A straight path with two endpoints (A________B)
  • Ray: Starts at one endpoint and continues forever in one direction (→)
  • Angle: Formed by two rays sharing the same endpoint (vertex)

examples.problem: What geometry term describes the tip of a pencil?
examples.solution: A point. A point marks an exact location with no size.

examples.problem: Which goes on forever in one direction: a line segment or a ray?
examples.solution: A ray. It starts at a point and extends forever in one direction.

examples.problem: The corner of a book models what geometry term?

recap: Point = dot (no size). Line segment = 2 endpoints. Ray = 1 endpoint, goes forever.
Line segment is part of a line; ray is half a line.

topics.title: Classify Angles: Right, Acute, Obtuse
topics.concept:
Angles are classified by their size (measured in degrees °):

  • Right angle: Exactly 90° — looks like a perfect corner (L shape)
  • Acute angle: Less than 90° — smaller than a right angle (sharp, narrow)
  • Obtuse angle: More than 90° — larger than a right angle (wide, blunt)

A small square symbol in the corner means it is a right angle.

examples.problem: What angle is at the corner of a square?
examples.solution: A right angle (90°). All four corners of a square are right angles.

examples.problem: A slightly open book makes a sharp angle. What type is it?
examples.solution: Acute angle — less than 90°, narrow and sharp.

examples.problem: A wide-open door makes a large angle. What type is it?
examples.solution: Obtuse angle — more than 90°, wide and open.

recap: Right = exactly 90° (square corner). Acute = less than 90° (sharp). Obtuse = more than 90° (wide).
Compare to the corner of a piece of paper: that is 90°.
Acute is smaller than right; obtuse is bigger than right.

quiz.q: A corner of a square is a ___ angle.

questions.q: A dot showing an exact location is called a?
questions.explanation: A point is an exact location shown as a dot.

questions.q: A straight path with two endpoints is a?
questions.explanation: A line segment has exactly two endpoints.

questions.q: A ray starts at a ___ and goes on forever.
questions.explanation: A ray starts at one point (endpoint) and extends forever in one direction.

questions.q: The corner of a book represents a?
questions.explanation: The corner of a book is a right angle (exactly 90°).
45° is less than 90°, so it is an acute angle.
120° is more than 90°, so it is an obtuse angle.

questions.q: Two rays with the same endpoint form an?
questions.explanation: An angle is formed by two rays that share the same endpoint (vertex).

questions.q: Which angle is smallest: acute, right, or obtuse?
questions.explanation: Acute < Right (90°) < Obtuse. So acute is smallest.

questions.q: Which angle is largest: acute, right, or obtuse?
questions.explanation: Obtuse > Right (90°) > Acute. So obtuse is largest.

questions.q: How many right angles does a square have?
questions.explanation: A square has 4 corners, each a right angle (90°).

questions.q: Is 89° an acute or obtuse angle?
questions.explanation: 89° is just less than 90°, so it is an acute angle.

questions.q: Is 91° an acute or obtuse angle?
questions.explanation: 91° is just more than 90°, so it is an obtuse angle.

questions.q: A clock at 3:00 — what angle do the hands form?
questions.explanation: At 3:00 the minute hand points at 12 and hour hand at 3 — making a perfect right angle (90°).

questions.q: A clock at 5:00 — what type of angle do the hands form?
questions.explanation: At 5:00 the angle between hands is 150° (5 x 30° per hour), which is obtuse.

questions.q: How many angles in a triangle?
questions.explanation: A triangle has 3 sides and 3 angles.
